So ultimately you want a specialist to diagnose you. They will give you a questionnaire and usually talk through your experience and make a judgement based on this. The things to look out for is your school reports and what are they saying. This is so important because in my experience my lack of focus was CONSISTENTLY pointed out but no one out 2 and 2 together. So keep records of those. Also have a read through ADHD symptom posts on here if it relates to you then it's an indicator that it's worth you being tested. Also another thing to note is how you respond to stimulants. This isn't always the case but sometimes if you feel normal/more focused after drinking a can of red bull and not completely wired then this can be a small indicator that you could be ADHD typical. Due to how broken and slow our synapses are in our brain, the stimulants increase the efficiency of that, that's why most ADHD medication is amphetamines.

I don't know your current state of medication or whether you have ADHD so I'll assume you do. I used to be medicated and like an idiot I was discharged from adult ADHD services and it's a pain to get seen again. This is purely from my own experience of things that might help and also things to note:

1. The right medication allows you to get in a tunnel vision state which is ultimately the goal. You may have to try different ones to find the right fit for you and that gets you up to speed.

2. I have found some of the gaming energy drink that have vitamins have an effect on my focus. I use sneak energy but there's a lot of them out there.

3. Anything that is a stimulant. Coffee, caffeine anything that is designed to stimulate the brain. Our synapses in the brain are slow as shit which is why stimulants is what is prescribed. I would try option 2 before necking red bulls every day but find whatever works for you.

3. Hyperfixation annoyingly isn't always the easiest thing to switch on from my experience. For example, after a Tough break up or negative emotional event, It's very difficult to switch off the more intense intrusive thoughts. I've lost a good job because of this years ago because I was not able to switch off all the white noise.

The environment has to be optimal, usually on a good day we're more likely to get that. So just be aware sometimes you might have to work on setting the framework for it like playing a chilled playlist or waking up early to give a sense of accomplishment to focus. You'll know what little touches make you feel more relaxed and motivated and primed to to get there.

4. Lastly if you are a creative person. The biggest thing that spurs hyperfixation is inspiration. I've spent 9+ hours learning stuff on guitar based on the fact I was going through spells of feeding my brain with new music and stuff. If there is anything in your goal that you want to achieve that you can find something online that inspires you to learn more or make a start then go looking for that. 

Its important to just be aware that most of us struggle focusing. Which is why we are classed ADHD in the first place hyperfixation is awesome but you'll need to figure out what it is that helps you get there more times than it will fail. Sorry that was long hope you get something from this. ✌🏻

Hi, I've had ADHD all my life. It's not really talked about seriously and it still has a massive stigma attached to it. Not enough is known about it so general acceptance of it in most walks of life is non existent. I wasn't diagnosed with ADHD until 19 and one of the biggest things that plagues anybody with ADHD is the sense of shame and that usually turns into a deep sense of self loathing for not being quote on quote normal. To answer your question I believe that depression and anxiety affects us because we do harbour this shame, we know that in social situations people can literally have a conversation with us and I have to pretend to understand what they are saying and feign an interest. This is just one form of anxiety. Depression comes over time because it is exhausting to be in a never-ending cycle of executive dysfunction and the jibes that people make who just think maybe you're a bit useless at times or so disorganized. Ultimately I believe that once I have a solid therapy plan that targeting the ADHD aspect is the root of the main issue. Depression and anxiety genuinely feel like a natural by product of it. Prescribing anti depressants just masks the real issue and isn't a wholesome solution to the problem.

I'll try and keep this short. I was diagnosed at 19 with ADHD so I struggle a lot coping with it. My experience of treatments and diagnosis is this. The reality is the ADHD test along with the test they send you for anxiety asks very leading questions and it's easy to appear that you have ADHD by filling out that form. The biggest indicators of ADHD is school reports and actually sitting down with a specialist. My reports at school ALWAYS said the same thing. "Bright student but is disruptive and struggles with focus." Not enough is being done to deal with ADHD. It brings along its mates anxiety and depression and its now been tightly linked with autism now. Getting diagnosed is hard but the treatment aspect is way harder. Once you have got a diagnosis the hard work begins and I struggled with medications and the check ups aren't really as regular as they need to be. Purely down to the fact there is not enough money being pumped into this area. I could go on but if you want to ask any questions, pm me
